items.title: Implement the confidence route and build artifact
items.description: Implement the build-time confidence route so the calendar artifact makes one deterministic Merge/Group/Separate decision for every event listing. The route operates on cleaned events, never deletes a row because of similarity, and emits versioned duplicate-group IDs and diagnostics downstream consumers can trust. Done when: exact-title Merge uses the full cleaned title, compatible non-empty locations, deterministic survivor selection, and no similarity-edge propagation; Group uses same-instant connected components, the agreed guards and threshold, versioned IDs, bounded comparisons, and structured source aggregation; Separate stays authoritative and NULL group membership means one row is one group downstream; missing source_uid and route invariants fail closed with actionable diagnostics; the pure-route, ICS-boundary, false-merge, chain, truncation, instant, all-day, location, source-name, determinism, and blast-radius tests pass; and the generated event artifact contains the route output and per-event outcomes needed by later tickets. See the issue for the full acceptance criteria.
items.notes: Added the pure confidence_route() to scripts/ics_to_json.py (ROUTE_VERSION=cr1, threshold 0.80, guards ON) plus clean_title/normalize_route_title, split location predicates (both-present for Merge, or-empty for Group), variant/all-day guards, structured_source_names, deterministic survivor (primary-first, smallest uid, smallest url), versioned group ids, and validate_route_result() failing closed on missing source_uid, deletion without an exact-title survivor, duplicate survivors, malformed groups, and component/comparison budgets (25 / 250k). ics_to_json now runs the route on cleaned events, writes duplicate_group into events.json, and writes an events.route.json sidecar with per-event outcomes; cluster_id is left as a None passthrough and combine_ics title dedup is untouched (later items). similarity_test.py now imports the one canonical token-set function. 37 new tests in tests/test_confidence_route.py cover the pure route, ICS boundary (encoded-title merge), guards, chain/truncation/instant/all-day/location/source-name, determinism, and a real 1,029-listing blast-radius fixture. Full Python suite 290 pass, node 220 pass, pnpm bench pass, ruff and all four type checkers clean. Decisions: differing US state tokens make locations explicitly incompatible; deleted merge members carry duplicate_group=None with survivor_uid for tracing.

items.title: Persist duplicate groups and expose the authoritative view
items.description: Persist the route's duplicate-group decision and expose it through the authoritative deduplicated read model. Done when: the database stores nullable duplicate_group and stores the route output; the materialized view groups by stored group ID and isolates every NULL row instead of collapsing NULLs together; grouped rows aggregate member IDs, structured source URLs, source names, and representative fields deterministically; the event loader persists the field without breaking existing upsert and stale-event behavior; migration, grants, indexes, refresh behavior, and database tests are complete; and materialized-view refresh failures fail the pipeline.
items.notes: Landed persistence + the authoritative view. Migration supabase/migrations/20260922120000_add_duplicate_group_and_route_view.sql adds nullable events.duplicate_group plus source_names text[] and duplicate_group_representative text, and recreates deduplicated_events to group by (city, start_time, coalesce(duplicate_group, 'row:'||id)) so every NULL row is its own group; the view unions merged_ids, source_urls (jsonb), and structured source names, and presents the route's representative id/fields instead of min(id). The route now persists source_names (ordered, primaries first) and duplicate_group_representative (min by aggregator-priority, source_uid, url); validate_route_result fails closed on a group without exactly one member representative or a Separate row declaring one. Also fixed structured_source_names so a lone human source name is not overridden by a divergent ICS-assembly url-map key (slug fallback); comma-joined strings still defer to the url map. Loader needs no change: load-events upserts whole event objects, so the new columns persist automatically and delete_stale_events is untouched (its pgTAP suite still passes). The refresh-failure criterion was already met by the existing non-continue-on-error 'Refresh deduplicated events' workflow step. Tests: 7 new Python route tests plus supabase/tests/test_deduplicated_events.sql (22 pgTAP assertions); 298 pytest, 220 vitest, 41 pgTAP, ruff + 4 type checkers, prettier/eslint, pnpm bench, and validate_pr_feeds all green on a fresh supabase db reset. Decisions (unattended, pre-approved): added the two extra columns beyond the spec's earlier 'only duplicate_group' schema line because the 2026-09-22 review amendment requires structured source names and the route's representative rather than min(id). Observation for review: 15/1027 fixture rows whose human source name itself contains a comma fall back to the slug url-map key (e.g. 'Events Livewhale 11'); root cause is combine_ics get_source_name's slug fallback feeding X-SOURCE-URLS, not the view; candidate follow-up.

items.title: Switch calendar, dashboard, and picks to stored groups
items.description: Switch the main calendar, dashboard tiles, and saved-picks experience to the stored deduplicated read model so each Group renders once while every member source and pick remains available. Done when: all relevant REST projections include duplicate_group and merged_ids; the main calendar and dashboard consume the authoritative deduplicated view rather than raw-event fallback logic; NULL groups remain separate in the client; grouped cards retain deterministic representative presentation and every member source link; picking or unpicking a Group covers all IDs in merged_ids; My Picks and the Pick Editor show no duplicate representations of one Group; and client, browser, and database seam tests pass.
items.notes: Switched the client consumers to the stored route decision. helpers.dedupeEvents now keys on (start_time, duplicate_group): a non-NULL group collapses, a NULL group is one row is one group keyed by row id (the title+time fallback is gone), membership is seeded from the view's merged_ids, source_urls are unioned, and the sort uses duplicate_group instead of cluster_id. clusterBorder now hashes the opaque duplicate_group id (pinned colour test) and returns none for NULL/filtered. New helpers.eventMergedIds (camelCase mergedIds -> view merged_ids -> [id]) feeds EventCard pick state and Globals.togglePick, which now clears every pick in the group on unpick; new helpers.dedupePicks collapses My Picks to one row per stored group (canonical representative preferred, identity-cached) for both the list and its count. shell.js's deduplicated_events projection gained duplicate_group (merged_ids was already selected); FeedTile switched from the raw events table to deduplicated_events with duplicate_group/merged_ids/source_urls, so dashboard tiles and the main list read the same view. The my-picks ICS feed was treated as part of the saved-picks experience: its projection gained source_uid/duplicate_group/duplicate_group_representative and it collapses picked members to one entry per stored group via new dedupe.ts. Tests: 19 vitest in tests/js/validate-dedupe-groups.test.js (group collapse, NULL separate, different stored groups stay separate, mergedIds seeding, clusterBorder pin, eventMergedIds, dedupePicks representative preference, plus source-contract assertions for the shell/FeedTile/EventCard/Main projections); the shipped xmlui/test.html harness's old title-fallback dedupe tests were rewritten to the stored-group + NULL-separate contract; 3 Deno tests in supabase/functions/my-picks/dedupe_test.ts. Verified: 298 pytest, 239 vitest, 25 Playwright, 41 pgTAP (supabase test db), ruff + 4 type checkers, prettier/eslint, pnpm bench, and deno check all green. Decisions (unattended, pre-approved): dedupe the my-picks feed too and extract dedupe.ts so the test imports without booting Deno.serve; keep cluster_id readable in the view (compatibility window, removed in a later item). Observation for review: the Deno edge-function test runs locally (deno test supabase/functions/my-picks/dedupe_test.ts) but is not wired into make test or CI because the repo has no Deno harness; candidate follow-up for #155 or the review.

items.title: Make RSS consume stored group decisions
items.description: Make RSS consume the stored route decisions so each Group renders once, uses the same canonical representative as the app, and does not repeatedly announce suppressed members as new. Done when: RSS does not recompute similarity, location, or grouping; full and latest feeds render one item per stored Group; new-item state considers all current member UIDs, including members suppressed from rendering; repeated builds with unchanged membership produce no false new-item announcements; and RSS uses the route's canonical representative with tests covering representative and membership changes.
items.notes: generate_rss.py is now a pure consumer of the stored route decision. New group_key keys a non-NULL duplicate_group as one Group and a NULL group as one row is one group (per-row key, so Separate rows never collapse). group_upcoming collapses each Group to one feed entry whose representative is the route's duplicate_group_representative (a Separate row is its own; a missing declared representative falls back to smallest GUID), and each entry carries every member GUID. Both feeds render one item per Group. Suppressed members are emitted as <category> UIDs on the item, and read_feed_state now returns the union of item GUIDs and category UIDs as known_uids, so the next build's new-item test (members <= prev_full_known) sees all current member UIDs including suppressed ones: an unchanged membership carries its first-seen pubDate and never re-announces, while a newly joining member stamps now and is announced even when the representative GUID is already known. main() delegates to a testable generate(city, events, outdir, state_dir, now) with injected clock/state. No similarity, location, or grouping logic is recomputed. New tests/test_generate_rss.py (6 tests) drive two consecutive builds through the written XML: one item per stored Group, NULL rows separate, stored-decision-not-similarity, unchanged-membership no re-announce, new-member announced, representative change not re-announced. Verified: 304 pytest, 239 vitest, 25 Playwright, 41 pgTAP, pnpm bench, validate_pr_feeds, ruff + all four type checkers clean. Decision (unattended, pre-approved): member UIDs ride on standard RSS <category> elements because the state model keeps no storage beyond the feeds themselves; this is the minimal self-contained way for a later build to know about suppressed members.

items.title: Complete compatibility transition and integration verification
items.description: Complete the compatibility transition so duplicate_group is the only active grouping authority, legacy cluster_id has a bounded compatibility window, and the full repository passes the integrated route, database, frontend, RSS, and performance checks. Done when: all active consumers use duplicate_group; cluster_id remains only for the explicitly allowed compatibility build and has no competing producer; performance, pipeline, frontend, database, RSS, and full-artifact checks pass together; a separately verified cleanup migration removes unused cluster_id behavior after no consumer remains; and the domain glossary and ADR documentation record the final Merge/Group/Separate model.
items.notes: Completed the cluster_id transition and integration verification. Removed the retired cluster_by_title_similarity() (the only competing cluster_id producer; it was already uncalled) and dropped the cluster_id key from the ics_to_json artifact so the loader never sees the dead field. shell.js's deduplicated_events projection no longer selects cluster_id. New cleanup migration supabase/migrations/20260922130000_drop_cluster_id.sql drops events.cluster_id and recreates the authoritative deduplicated_events view without it (same grouping/NULL-isolation/representative semantics; indexes, grants, and refresh_deduplicated_events preserved); supabase/ddl/02_events.sql and 17_deduplicated_events.sql updated to match the live state. Docs: CONTEXT.md gains glossary entries (Listing, Merge, Group, Separate, duplicate group) and a rewritten Deduplication entry pointing at ADR 0013-confidence-route-merge-group-separate.md, which records the two-band destructive/non-destructive route, the exact-title Merge equivalence class, the versioned group id, the retired cluster_id, and the deliberate absence of a same-source guard; docs/pipeline.md's dedup section and docs/deduplication.md's header now reflect the route (the latter keeps its pre-route stages under a superseded banner). Durable tests left behind: tests/test_confidence_route.py::TestIcsBoundary::test_artifact_omits_retired_cluster_id (build artifact), tests/js/validate-dedupe-groups.test.js 'no longer carries the retired cluster_id field' (client projection), and supabase/tests/test_cluster_id_retired.sql (events/view columns absent; view still collapses a stored Group and unions sources without the column). Verified together on a fresh supabase db reset: make check (305 pytest, 240 vitest, ruff + all four type checkers, prettier/eslint), supabase test db (45 pgTAP, up from 41), pnpm bench PASS, pnpm playwright test (25 passed), validate_pr_feeds (no feed changes). Decisions (unattended, pre-approved): close the compatibility window now rather than leave the column for another cycle, because no consumer reads it and the only REST projection that named it is updated in the same change; keep the pre-route docs/deduplication.md stages under a 'Superseded' banner instead of rewriting the whole historical doc. Skipped: scripts/validate_pipeline.py needs built cities/*/events.json artifacts (none in this worktree) and is documented as not-needed-per-PR; no scraper/feed/pipeline code was touched. Observation for the review: combine_ics.dedupe_cross_source still runs a title+date cross-source merge before the route (the spec's 'combine_ics keeps only UID-level de-duplication' wording), so it remains a pre-route merge layer; left for the review ticket rather than broadening this scope.

items.title: Review the work against the spec
items.description: Run the `code-review` skill over `git diff b188ccd379923e2286e152c0dfdbc8ce98cc22cf...HEAD` (the diff since this scope was seeded) against the spec at `.scratch/150-dedup-confidence-route/spec-150.md`, reviewing the implementation of #150 and its sub-tickets. Run the findings through `receiving-code-review`, then append each worthwhile finding as a new item with no `reference`, `hand_off: false`, and a `priority` greater than this item's. Write every remaining finding and every outstanding hand-off item into this item's `notes`. The HITL item (#156) is placed after this review by design, not by oversight: a person approves the production build only once the review findings are resolved, so this review is the last gating item before the hand-off.
items.notes: Ran the code-review skill over `git diff b188ccd379923e2286e152c0dfdbc8ce98cc22cf...HEAD` (5 commits, 31 files) against `.scratch/150-dedup-confidence-route/spec-150.md`, with the Standards and Spec axes as parallel sub-agents; verified every finding against the code (read/grep) and ran the set through receiving-code-review. Gate green on this commit: `make check` = 305 pytest, 240 vitest, ruff + all four type checkers clean. Accepted findings appended as new items with no reference, hand_off false, priorities 7-12: (7) combine_ics.dedupe_cross_source still runs a title+date pre-route merge, so a destructive fuzzy layer survives upstream of the audited exact-title band (spec L105); (8) the location guard implements only US-state incompatibility, not the amendment's city-token rule, so two same-state cities sharing a street number and tokens compare compatible and could Merge (spec amendment L401); (9) the client still splits and reorders comma-joined source text and shell.js omits source_names, violating "source names are never recovered by splitting ambiguous comma-separated text" and the single-representative rule (L402/L388); (10) the cluster_id consumer switch and drop migration ship together, collapsing the one-compatibility-build window the spec required (L409); (11) the blast-radius test uses a 1,029-listing slice, not the spec's 8,573-event full artifact, and records no full-artifact baseline (L311); (12) docs contradict the code (CONTEXT.md group-id format `cr1:<hash>` vs the emitted `cr1-<hash>`; dedupeEvents header still says same title + start_time; fixtures README omits the confidence_route fixture). Findings evaluated and NOT ticketed, with reasoning: RSS render_item still appends `Source: {source}` to its description but the line is identical at the fixed point b188ccd (pre-existing, not introduced here) and AGENTS.md's rule addresses stored event descriptions feeding a UI that renders source separately, while the RSS reader has no separate source element; Speculative Generality on the guard options is rejected because Testing Decisions explicitly require each guard to change the outcome when disabled and the amendments require explicit guard defaults; Divergent Change / moving the route to its own module is rejected because spec L126 says "No new module"; Middle Man (clean_title is a pass-through of clean_text) and Primitive Obsession (stringly outcome/group id) are minor judgement calls recorded here; the full deduplicated_events definition repeated across migrations and DDL is accepted as inherent to self-contained migrations plus DDL-as-documentation; and the duplicated group-key literal across client/RSS/SQL is inherent to three runtimes, with its substantive part (the client's competing source ordering) covered by item 9. Outstanding hand-off item for the human: #156 "HITL: Deploy, observe, and approve the first production build" (priority 100, hand_off true) gates production rollout, not completion of this scope.

items.title: Retire the pre-route title-based merge in combine_ics
items.description: Spec-150 line 105: "combine_ics.dedupe_cross_source's title-based passes are retired; combine_ics keeps only UID-level de-duplication and ICS assembly", and L63/L190 make the route the one place that decides whether two different listings are one event. scripts/combine_ics.py is untouched: dedupe_cross_source(uid_deduped, input_dir) still runs its title+date merge (combine_ics.py:999, invoked by generate-calendar.yml) before the route, so a destructive fuzzy merge survives upstream of the audited exact-title band. Done when: combine_ics keeps only UID-level de-duplication and ICS assembly; its tests cover UID-level dedup only; and an integration test demonstrates no title-based deletion happens before the confidence route. Record the decision and evidence in the item notes.
items.notes: Retired the pre-route title-based merge. Removed dedupe_cross_source (title+date grouping, the "at Venue Name" prefix pass) plus its only helpers normalize_title (the 40-char normalization) and get_dedup_key; extracted the inline UID loop into a typed, testable dedupe_by_uid(events) and combine_ics_files now calls it. combine_ics is left with UID-level de-duplication and ICS assembly only, so a title match can no longer delete a row before the route sees it. Left dedupe_fuzzy in place: it is opt-in via ENABLE_FUZZY_DEDUP, off in generate-calendar.yml, and explicitly Out of Scope in spec-150 ("it stays disabled"). Tests: new tests/test_combine_ics.py — TestDedupeByUid pins that a repeated UID keeps only the first listing and that a missing UID is never dropped (fails closed upstream in the route, not silently here); TestNoTitleDeletionBeforeRoute drives the real combine_ics_files -> ics_to_json boundary with two same-title/same-instant source files, asserting the combined ICS keeps both VEVENTs and (a) the route keeps both as Separate when locations are incompatible, (b) the route alone deletes one when locations are compatible (merge_deleted == 1). Removed the now-invalid dedupe_cross_source tests from test_visit_bloomington.py and test_wfiu_community_calendar.py (the primary-source-over-aggregator preference is now the route's survivor rule, already covered by tests/test_confidence_route.py); kept the ADR 0011 "primary not an aggregator" registration assertions. Decision (unattended, pre-approved): extract dedupe_by_uid rather than test the loop through combine_ics_files only, because UID de-duplication is now the module's sole remaining dedup and deserves a focused seam; the integration test still covers the end-to-end contract. Verified on this commit: make check = 306 pytest (up from 305; +4 new, -3 retired) and 240 vitest, ruff + all four type checkers, prettier/eslint clean; validate_pr_feeds reports no feed/scraper changes. Docs already describe the new model (CONTEXT.md L190, docs/pipeline.md L110 say combine_ics performs UID-level de-duplication); docs/deduplication.md's dedupe_cross_source description sits under its existing "Superseded (2026-09-22)" banner and is retained as pre-route history, left for the docs-cleanup item.

items.title: Add the amendment's city-token location incompatibility
items.description: Spec-150 review amendment line 401 requires location comparison to include "explicit incompatibility for differing city tokens." scripts/ics_to_json.py::_locations_compatible implements only US-state incompatibility (_US_STATE_TOKENS) plus shared-token/street-number matching, so two same-state cities whose locations share a street name and number (e.g. "100 Main St, Bloomington, IN" vs "100 Main St, Indianapolis, IN") still compare compatible and an exact-title Merge could delete one. Done when: differing city/town tokens are explicitly incompatible; a fixture pins two same-state, same-street-number listings as Separate (not Merge); and the existing both-present vs or-empty location tests still pass. Keep the rule deterministic text-only, with no geocoding or network lookup.
items.notes: Added _city_token() to scripts/ics_to_json.py and wired it into _locations_compatible (so both locations_compatible_both and locations_compatible_or_empty inherit it, and validate_route_result's merge guard re-checks it): the city is the token immediately before the last recognised US-state token (positional, text-only, no gazetteer and no geocoding), and a pair with two extractable but differing city tokens is explicitly incompatible. The rule only fires when both sides name an extractable city, so locations with no state (e.g. 'Musical Arts Center & LIVE@jacobs') still fall back to the shared-token/street-number rules and keep merging with a state-bearing spelling of the same venue. This closes the amendment's gap where '100 Main St, Bloomington, IN' vs '100 Main St, Indianapolis, IN' shared 'main'/'street' and compared compatible. Tests written red first: TestPrimitives city-mismatch incompatible (both predicates) + same-city-spelled-differently ('IN' vs 'Indiana 47401') compatible; TestMerge::test_merge_requires_matching_city_tokens (same-state/same-street-number pair stays two rows, merge_deleted 0); TestIcsBoundary::test_same_street_number_across_cities_is_not_merged (full ics_to_json build keeps both rows, merge_deleted 0). Verified make check green: 310 pytest (up from 306, +4), 240 vitest, ruff + all four type checkers, prettier/eslint. Real blast-radius fixture counts unchanged (merge_classes 2, merge_deleted 2, groups 25, grouped_members 51, max_group_size 3). Decision (unattended, pre-approved): positional token-before-last-state-token extraction rather than a city list, because the amendment forbids geocoding and in US address formats that position is the town; multi-word-city last-word collisions (e.g. 'New York' vs 'New York City') under-detect and stay Separate, which is the safe non-destructive direction.

items.title: Consume structured source_names in the client
items.description: Spec-150 amendment line 402: source names stay structured while routing and aggregating and "source names are never recovered by splitting ambiguous comma-separated text"; L388 requires all consumers to use the same deterministic representative rather than a competing rule. xmlui/helpers.js::dedupeEvents still does (e.source || '').split(',') and re-sorts sources with its own aggregator/location heuristic, and xmlui/shell.js's deduplicated_events projection omits source_names, so a human source name containing a comma is split and re-ordered and the card can disagree with the view. Done when: shell.js selects source_names; dedupeEvents folds the view's ordered source_names instead of splitting source; the client's source order matches the view's representative ordering; and a vitest pins a comma-containing source name surviving unmangled through the card path.
items.notes: Consumed the route's structured source names on the client. shell.js's deduplicated_events projection and FeedTile's dashboard projection now select source_names; dedupeEvents folds the view's ordered source_names array (deduped, representative-first) instead of splitting the comma-joined compatibility `source` string, and only the raw-row fallback keeps the legacy aggregator/location sort, so a group's source order now matches the view's representative ordering. formatSourceLinks gained an optional fourth sourceNames argument and prefers it when present; EventCard and PickEditor pass $props.event.source_names so the card renders each name (including a comma-containing human name like 'Taste, Inc.') as one link. Tests: 6 new vitest in tests/js/validate-dedupe-groups.test.js — a comma name is not split, the view order is preserved over a re-sort, the comma name stays intact through dedupeEvents -> formatSourceLinks (the card path), the raw-row split fallback is retained, and source-contract assertions pin that shell.js/FeedTile select source_names and the card/pick editor pass it. Verified: make check = 310 pytest + 246 vitest, ruff + all four type checkers, prettier/eslint clean; pnpm bench PASS; pnpm playwright test 25 passed. Decision (unattended, pre-approved): FeedTile's projection also gains source_names even though the ticket named only shell.js, because FeedTile renders EventCard and reads the same view, so leaving it out would keep the dashboard splitting comma text. Observation for review: helpers.js::sortSourcesForDisplay and the source-count/hidden-filter helpers (filterHiddenSources, getSourceCounts, getVisibleSourceCounts) still derive names by splitting e.source; they are outside this ticket's named scope (dedupeEvents + shell.js + card path) but remain candidates if the review wants every client split site retired.

items.title: Verify the cluster_id compatibility window and drop ordering
items.description: Spec-150 review amendment line 409: "cluster_id remains readable for one compatibility build while all consumers move to duplicate_group; a separately verified cleanup migration then removes the legacy column." The consumer switch (a6beece24) and the drop migration (supabase/migrations/20260922130000_drop_cluster_id.sql, 8417fa6e7) ship in the same branch, so a normal deploy applies both together and no compatibility build reads the column. Done when: either the one-build compatibility window is restored, or the combined deployment ordering is verified (the drop migration lands before any build emits the retired field and load-events cannot receive cluster_id) and a durable test or documented check pins that ordering. Record the decision and evidence in notes.

items.title: Run the full-artifact blast-radius check and record the baseline
items.description: Spec-150 testing decisions line 311: "A fixture over the built events.json (8,573 events): record the merge/group counts as a baseline, assert every deleted row has an exact-title survivor in its bucket, and assert no group exceeds the observed max size." tests/test_confidence_route.py::TestBlastRadius uses only a 1,029-listing slice (tests/fixtures/confidence_route/bloomington_2026-09-21_27.json), and no full-artifact merge/group count is recorded. Done when: the blast-radius check runs against the real built events.json (or a fixture at the full event count), records the merge and group counts plus observed max group size, and asserts the deletion and size invariants; the resulting baseline is recorded in notes.

items.title: Correct docs that contradict the route code
items.description: The review found three documentation defects from this scope: (1) CONTEXT.md line 104 documents the duplicate-group id format as `cr1:<hash>` while scripts/ics_to_json.py::_group_id emits `cr1-<hash>` (ROUTE_VERSION + '-' + sha1 hex); (2) xmlui/helpers.js line 1334 still heads dedupeEvents with "merge events with same title + start_time", contradicting the stored-group key; (3) tests/fixtures/README.md scopes the directory to minimal ICS fixtures and omits the new tests/fixtures/confidence_route/ JSON fixture. Done when: all three read true against the code, and the fixtures README documents the route fixture's purpose.

items.title: HITL: Deploy, observe, and approve the first production build
items.description: Human-verify the production migration and first scheduled build before destructive Merge behavior is considered live. Done when: the Supabase migration, materialized-view contract, grants, and refresh permissions are verified in production; one production build completes with route diagnostics and expected refresh behavior; Merge/group counts, maximum group size, and invariant diagnostics are reviewed against the agreed safety budget; the main calendar, dashboard, saved picks, source links, and RSS are spot-checked for parity; and a human approves the observed blast radius or records required follow-up changes. This item follows the review by design: a person approves the production build only after the review findings are resolved.
